subject: Phased discount schedule & reseller waterfall — procurement constraints
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Phased discount schedule & reseller waterfall — procurement constraints

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation, we want to align on a private-offer structure that balances your internal procurement rules (list-price floor, multi-year TCV phasing) with the reseller margin your partners expect. A few concrete asks so we can produce a clean PO: 

1) Procurement constraints — can you confirm if Stellaris requires a single list-price on the invoice (no split lines) or if line-itemized pricing is acceptable?
2) Multi-year phasing — would a 3-year TCV with front-loaded discounts (higher in year 1, normalized thereafter) work, or does procurement demand an equalized annual price?
3) Reseller waterfall — do you need the reseller split to appear on the invoice, or is a separate commission reconciliation acceptable?

We can produce two options quickly: (A) front-loaded 18% discount Y1 / 8% Y2 / 5% Y3 with a 20% reseller pass-through cap, or (B) equalized 10%/10%/10% with a 15% pass-through and an escrowed uplift if usage exceeds committed bands. Which direction should we draft?

I attached a simple pricing grid so you can see the tokenized math. If you want a one-page MOU for procurement, we can spin that today.

Best,
Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Attachments: stellaris-pricing-grid-v3.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Priya Singh <priya@stellarishealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Cc: accounts-payable@stellarishealth.com
Date: Sun, 22 Apr 2028 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased discount schedule & reseller waterfall — procurement constraints

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear options. A few clarifications from procurement (copied AP):

- Invoice requirements: Our procurement team prefers line-itemized invoices showing list price, discount applied, and net charge. They do not accept off-invoice shadow adjustments.
- Multi-year: We normally aim for levelized annual charges to align with budget approvals, but will accept front-loaded if we capture the discount language clearly in the PO and amortization schedule.
- Reseller: Our reseller agreements require the reseller margin to be reflected in a separate commission schedule (not on the customer invoice). The marketplace private-offer can show the net to customer and we will handle partner commission via a separate settlement.

On the numbers — option A (front-loaded) is attractive for year 1 budget reasons, but I need to confirm with finance before committing to 18% Y1. One more ask: can Redwood provide an example DocuSign MOU with the phased schedule and an invoice sample? That speeds legal review.

Priya Singh
VP, Procurement | Stellaris Health
priya@stellarishealth.com

accounts-payable@stellarishealth.com attached: PO-template.pdf (attachment referenced)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Phased discount schedule & reseller waterfall — procurement constraints

Ben / team —

Thanks — capturing procurement asks. Quick internal notes and recommended approach before we send the MOU: 

- Invoice formatting: we can produce a line-itemized invoice in the private-offer with columns for list price, discount (explicit), and net. That aligns with their requirement to avoid off-invoice adjustments. Ops will need the SKU mapping for invoice template.
- Multi-year: propose drafting the MOU with front-loaded schedule but include an alternate equalized schedule as appendix (lets procurement pick). This prevents rework and keeps momentum.
- Reseller waterfall: because Stellaris requires commission outside the invoice, we'll include a "Reseller Settlement Schedule" (PDF attachment) that defines the 20% cap pass-through and conditions for uplift. That schedule will not be visible to the customer invoice but will be provided to the partner under NDA.

Action items for us:
1) Ben — prepare one-page MOU + invoice sample and attach the reseller settlement draft.
2) Karthik — validate tax/treatment of front-loaded credits (we need to confirm revenue recognition impact for accounting).
3) Connor — ops: create SKU-to-line-item mapping for their private-offer so billing shows the expected columns.

I've attached a quick reseller-waterfall-draft.pdf for review. If everyone signs off, Ben should send to Priya with DocuSign links.

Mina Haddad
Head of Deal Ops | Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.ai

Attachments: reseller-waterfall-draft.pdf (policy/sample)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Singh <priya@stellarishealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.ai>, accounts-payable@stellarishealth.com
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 13:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Phased discount schedule & reseller waterfall — procurement constraints

Hi Priya —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. Attached are the two items you asked for: (1) one-page MOU with both the front-loaded and levelized pricing tables, and (2) invoice sample that shows list price, explicit discount, and net line. I also attached the Reseller Settlement Schedule as Mina mentioned; it is packaged as a partner-only appendix and not shown on the invoice.

Key points in the MOU:
- Option A (recommended by Redwood): 18% Y1 / 8% Y2 / 5% Y3. This reduces your first-year effective cost and helps with initial deployment.
- Option B: Levelized 10%/10%/10% with a 15% reseller pass-through.
- If Stellaris chooses Option A, Redwood will provide a one-time adoption credit for the first 90 days (up to $25k) applied as a separate credit memo — this will be reflected as a credit line on the first invoice.

Next steps: if procurement is OK with the invoice format and the partner commission being on the separate schedule, we can send the DocuSign MOU today and target a May 15 start date.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Attachments: Redwood_MOU_Stellaris_Apr2028.docx (MOU stub), invoice-sample-stellaris.pdf (invoice sample), reseller-waterfall-draft.pdf
